phase: unreleased working-tree scene composition inheritance changes

observations: editOverrides requires its own edit capability; patchOverrides continues to require the unchanged patch capability.
An unavailable new capability rejects the new operation without disabling already available operations.
The GUI hides reset controls for older cores, and selecting a reset additionally gates current-session application on the edit capability.
The boundary verifies the old six-key shape or new seven-key shape, supported field names, nonempty intent, unique reset fields and disjoint set/reset fields.
The proposal excludes selected reset fields from its changed set values; application preparation validates disjointness again.
Dense finite JSON request checks still run before ABI dispatch.
An absent override or absent reset field cannot create an empty override through a reset-only request.
Zero changes require byte-identical returned content at the bridge.
The proposal rejects a reset-only intent that cannot change an authored override.
Removing the last values member removes exactly the selected actor override entry and retains the overrides array.
Changed paths follow the fixed six-field order and the override index from the input source.
The bridge compares the complete expected recipe semantics, so unrelated actor changes, container removal, reordering or identity changes cannot pass.
A successful receipt is re-expanded by the existing strict core operation after the first ABI dispatch completes; malformed source cannot pass by JSON equality alone.
Source/model identities, content digest and saved baseline are detached and bound before proposing.
Preparation recomputes the exact receipt from the current content and stable instance/placement/local actor key.
The existing parent and editor recheck the active source owner, load token, source epoch, baseline and current content before in-memory application.
The normal save baseline and disk cache remain unchanged during application; no author-file writer or World transaction is added.
Reset selection participates in the form signature and revision epoch; input changes or reset toggles invalidate approval.
Reset controls are available only for authored fields; selected fields are disabled, and their former valid values serve only as ignored proposal placeholders.
The GUI explicitly identifies displayed values as pre-restoration; candidate validation resolves actual inheritance instead of guessing it in the form.
Explicit no-image null is kept distinct from image inheritance.
Cancel, forced close, stale async validation, stale source ownership and capability loss keep application guarded.
New reset strings have matching English and Japanese translations and accessible pressed state plus field labels.

limitations: This report assesses the source snapshots listed above; later product source changes require a follow-up review.
No browser visual verification, full application regression, fresh packaged-resource probe, installer or Android-device verification was performed by this review.
Rust implementation tests, formatter, clippy and native build are recorded separately in core-tests.log, core-fmt.log, core-clippy.log and core-native-build.log.
